title: Eco-hydrology observation of Cikapundung riverbank in Indonesia
author: Dasapta Erwin Irawan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.igdcbs6

steps.title: Create Cikapundung polyline vector
steps.instruction: Use ArcMap 10.4.1 to digitise an on‑screen polyline of the Cikapundung river based on a Google Earth base map.

steps.title: Generate riparian buffer zones
steps.instruction: Provide buffer zones at distances of 100 m, 300 m, and 500 m from the river body, extending from upstream to downstream.

steps.title: Classify land‑cover categories
steps.instruction: Using Google Earth imagery downloaded on 15 Nov 2016, classify land cover within the buffers into nine classes: forests; shrubs and bushes; fields; fields; grasslands; constructed land; industrial buildings; water bodies.

steps.title: Segment map and plot histograms
steps.instruction: Divide the mapped observation into segments each 3.6 km long and visualise the segment‑wise land‑cover results as histograms.

steps.title: Compute NDVI raster
steps.instruction: Transform the vegetation index to the Near‑Infrared/Visible‑Red band ratio, producing an NDVI band with values ranging from –1 to +1; values near 0 indicate little green vegetation, values near +1 indicate dense green vegetation.

steps.title: Calculate Kappa accuracy
steps.instruction: Build an error matrix (as in Table 3.1) and compute Cohen’s Kappa to assess agreement between digital classification and field ground‑truth data.

steps.title: Derive landscape metrics
steps.instruction: Calculate landscape metrics that quantify spatial structure, composition, and configuration of the classified land‑cover.

steps.title: Define vegetation plot
steps.instruction: Establish observation plots of 20 m × 5 m oriented parallel to the river length.

steps.title: Record tree diameters
steps.instruction: Within each plot, record all trees with diameters ≥ 10 cm.

steps.title: Measure edaphic parameters
steps.instruction: Using a portable soil tester, auger, and core sampler, measure soil pH, organic content, mineral content, and bulk density.

steps.title: Collect and weigh core soil sample
steps.instruction: Prepare and extract a soil core, then weigh fresh and dry masses.

substeps.instruction: Clean the ground surface of grass and litter.
Place the core sampler on the ground.
Draw a circle around the sampler with a radius twice that of the sampler.
Excavate a hole 10 cm deep within the circle to facilitate insertion.
Insert the core sampler vertically and tap gently until fully seated.
Cut the soil beneath the sampler with a shovel or knife.
Level the sampler mouth with a thin blade or nylon thread.
Store the intact soil core in a box to avoid damage.
Immediately weigh the core on an analytical balance (accuracy 0.01 g).
Dry the sample in an oven at 105 °C for 24 h.
Re‑weigh to obtain the constant dry weight.

steps.title: Laboratory analysis of soil
steps.instruction: Perform organic content and mineral analyses on the dried soil.

substeps.instruction: Using an auger, collect approximately 10 g of horizon A soil (0–10 cm depth) into a sealed container of known weight.
Oven‑dry at 105 °C to constant weight, then cool and weigh the dry mass.
Take 5 g of the dry soil and place it in a pre‑weighed dry porcelain crucible.
Fire the crucible in a furnace at 450 °C for 4 h.
Cool the crucible in a desiccator and weigh the final residue.
